nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with field of fractions $K$, and let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$. For a nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, let $v_{\mathfrak p}(I) \in \mathbb Z$ be the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of $I$ into prime ideals, with $v_{\mathfrak p}(0) = 0$. Then $v_{\mathfrak p}(I) \neq 0$ for only finitely many nonzero prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $A$.
nodes.title: Fractional ideals have finite support

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. For every finitely supported function $e$ from the height-one primes of $R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$ and every height-one prime $v$ of $R$, the $v$-adic valuation of the fractional ideal $\prod_w w^{e(w)}$, the product over the primes $w$ with $e(w) \neq 0$, equals $e(v)$.
nodes.title: Valuations of a product of prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain, let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $A$ and let $I$ be a nonzero ideal of $A$. Then the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of $I$ into prime ideals is zero if and only if $I \not\subseteq \mathfrak p$.
nodes.title: Vanishing multiplicity of a prime factor

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a maximal ideal of $R$, and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ a local ring that is a localization of $R$ at $\mathfrak p$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Then for every ideal $I$ of $R$, the multiplicity of $\mathfrak m$ in the extended ideal $I R_{\mathfrak p}$ equals the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in $I$. nodes.title: Ideal multiplicity is unchanged by localization at a maximal ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$ and let $w$ be a height-one prime of $R$. The factorization isomorphism sends the fractional ideal $w$, as a unit fractional ideal of $R$ in $K$, to the function on height-one primes of $R$ that is $1$ at $w$ and $0$ elsewhere.
nodes.title: Exponent function of a prime ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and for a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ and a height-one prime $v$ of $R$ write $\operatorname{val}_v(I)$ for the $v$-adic valuation of $I$. The factorization isomorphism is the group isomorphism from the unit group of the fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$ to the additive group of finitely supported functions from the height-one primes of $R$ to…
nodes.title: Prime factorization isomorphism for fractional ideals

nodes.summary: In a Dedekind domain $A$, every nonzero ideal $I$ is contained in only finitely many prime ideals of $A$.
nodes.title: Finitely many primes contain a nonzero ideal

nodes.summary: In a Dedekind domain $A$, every nonzero element $a$ lies in only finitely many prime ideals of $A$.
nodes.title: Finitely many primes contain a nonzero element

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. For every finitely supported function $e$ from the height-one primes of $R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$, the fractional ideal $\prod_v v^{e(v)}$ of $R$ in $K$, the product over the primes $v$ with $e(v) \neq 0$, is nonzero.
nodes.title: Products of prime powers are nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. For a finitely supported function $e$ from the height-one primes of $R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$, this is the fractional ideal $\prod_v v^{e(v)}$ of $R$ in $K$, the product over the primes $v$ with $e(v) \neq 0$, regarded as a unit of the monoid of fractional ideals (it is nonzero, hence invertible).
nodes.title: Fractional ideal with prescribed prime exponents

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $w$ be a height-one prime of $R$ and let $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. The inverse of the factorization isomorphism sends the function on height-one primes of $R$ that is $n$ at $w$ and $0$ elsewhere to the fractional ideal $w^n$.
nodes.title: Inverse factorization of a single prime power

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and for a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ and a height-one prime $v$ of $R$ write $\operatorname{val}_v(I)$ for the $v$-adic valuation of $I$. Every unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ equals $\prod_v v^{\operatorname{val}_v(I)}$, the product over the height-one primes $v$ of $R$ with $\operatorname{val}_v(I) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Reconstructing a fractional ideal from its prime exponents

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and let $e$ be a finitely supported function from the height-one primes of $R$ to $\mathbb{Z}$. The prime-exponent function of the fractional ideal $\prod_w w^{e(w)}$, the product over the primes $w$ with $e(w) \neq 0$, is $e$: its $v$-adic valuation is $e(v)$ for every height-one prime $v$ of $R$.
nodes.title: Recovering prime exponents from a product of prime powers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. For a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$, this is the finite set of height-one primes $v$ of $R$ at which the $v$-adic valuation of $I$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: Support of the prime exponents of a fractional ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and for a unit fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $K$ and a height-one prime $v$ of $R$ write $\operatorname{val}_v(I)$ for the $v$-adic valuation of $I$. For all unit fractional ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$ in $K$ and every height-one prime $v$ of $R$, $\operatorname{val}_v(IJ) = \operatorname{val}_v(I) + \operatorname{val}_v(J)$.
nodes.title: Prime exponents are additive

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and let $I$ be a unit of the monoid of fractional ideals of $R$ in $K$. nodes.title: Prime exponents of an invertible fractional ideal

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
